title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, from pages 97 to 99. Grothendieck works with an abstract 'disjunction' structure on a set E: a symmetric relation x|∘|y read as 'x and y are disjoint', i.e. an orthogonality space in the sense of Dacey and Foulis–Randall. To it he associates a 'space' Σ_E, which can be read as the complete lattice of biorthogonally closed subsets. Σ_E carries a complementation C (orthocomplement) and an induced disjunction relation. In the trivial case (x|∘|y iff x≠y), Σ_E = P(E) and C is the ordinary set complement.

Page 97 compared two notions of correspondence from E to E'. One is a relation R ⊂ E×E' with R(x) ∈ Σ_{E'} and ᵗR(x') ∈ Σ_E. The other is a closed subset of the 'product disposant' E×E', where (x,x')|∘|(y,y') iff x|∘|y or x'|∘|y'. He suspected the two agree only in the trivial case.

This page takes the intrinsic, lattice-theoretic view. Corr(Σ,Σ') is the set of maps Σ→Σ' commuting with arbitrary Sup, ordered pointwise: f ≤ g iff f(x) ≤ g(x) for all x ∈ Σ.

Claim 1. Corr(Σ,Σ') is a complete lattice, and Sup_i f_i is computed pointwise. The proof sketch is 'associativity of Sups': (Sup_i f_i)(Sup_j x_j) = Sup_i Sup_j f_i(x_j) = Sup_j Sup_i f_i(x_j). So the pointwise sup again commutes with Sup and is a correspondence. Arbitrary Inf then exist formally.

Claim 2. It is unclear how to equip Corr(Σ,Σ') with a complementation C or a disjunction structure, so that it would again be a 'space' of the same kind.

Claim 3. When E is trivial (Σ_E = P(E)), a Sup-preserving map is determined freely by its values on singletons. Hence Corr(Σ_E,Σ') ≅ Σ'^E. Then C and the disjunction relation can be defined componentwise: (Cf)(x) = C(f(x)) for x ∈ E. This makes Corr a product of copies of Σ'.

Page 99 continues. On arbitrary arguments A ∈ P(E), pointwise C fails: (Cf)(A) ≠ C(f(A)). He concludes that defining C on Corr in general seems tied to the existence of 'points' (minimal nonzero elements, i.e. atoms) or some substitute.

The problem served is internal-hom / closedness for his category of 'spaces': is Corr(Σ,Σ') again an object of the same type?
errors: Inf in Corr(Σ,Σ') exist, but they are NOT computed pointwise in general. The pointwise Inf of Sup-preserving maps need not preserve Sup. The text only says the Inf exist, which is correct, but a reader might over-read the pointwise formula as applying to Inf too.
Minor: Sup-preservation should include the empty Sup (f(0)=0). The pointwise argument handles this automatically.

The isomorphism Corr(P(E),Σ') ≅ Σ'^E is correct. Pointwise C on Σ'^E gives the product ortholattice, but this C depends on the chosen generating points, which is exactly the issue noted on the next page.

ideas.what: Join-preserving maps between complete lattices form a complete lattice with pointwise joins (internal hom of complete lattices)
ideas.modern_name: Internal hom in the category Sup of sup-lattices (monoidal closed structure)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical lattice theory; Joyal–Tierney (1984) for the monoidal closed category Sup

ideas.what: Orthogonality ('disjunction') structure on a set and its associated complete lattice of closed subsets with complementation C; trivial disjunction gives P(E)
ideas.modern_name: Orthogonality spaces / Dacey spaces and their ortholattices of biorthogonally closed sets

ideas.what: Free extension: for a powerset domain, Corr(P(E),Σ') ≅ Σ'^E with componentwise complementation
ideas.modern_name: P(E) as the free sup-lattice on E; product ortholattice

ideas.what: Problem of putting an orthocomplementation on the hom-object between ortholattices, linked to the existence of atoms ('points')
ideas.modern_name: Non-closedness of categories of orthomodular/ortho lattices; tensor product problem in quantum logic
ideas.usually_credited_to: Foulis–Randall, Aerts–Daubechies (c. 1978-81) on tensor products in quantum logic

missed.claim: Grothendieck independently arrives, in 1986, at the framework of orthogonality spaces and their complete ortholattices, i.e. quantum-logic-style 'spaces'. He runs into the known obstruction to a closed or tensor structure: no natural complementation on the hom of sup-maps except in the atomistic/powerset case. This links his 'spaces' programme to quantum logic, where the analogous non-existence results are known, though no reference to that literature appears.
missed.quote: Mais la structure C, ou la structure de disjonction, n'est pas claire.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly of historical interest: it documents Grothendieck's late foundational explorations of a pointless notion of 'space' with negation. The mathematics itself is known from Foulis–Randall and sup-lattice theory.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on this page is routine: pointwise sups of join-preserving maps, and the free sup-lattice on a set. Mildly notable is that Grothendieck in 1986 is reconstructing orthogonality-space and ortholattice theory and hitting the hom/tensor obstruction known in quantum logic. This seems undocumented in the literature on his work, but it is not new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: The word read as 'spatios' may be 'espaces' (a 'corr. d'espaces'); the handwriting is ambiguous.
'disjoncteur trivial' versus 'disposant trivial': the previous page's transcription uses 'disposant'. The word likely denotes the same notion (a set with a disjunction relation); verify consistency.
'l'application des seconds' is unclear and may refer to 'l'application des Sup', i.e. the pointwise-sup map; meaning uncertain.
The header has a small 'gp' annotation above 'déf', likely an editorial mark; the page number '101' appears bottom left.
